purpose: Section 23: before implementing the safe-failure architecture, map where material claims are dropped/withheld/unresolved/unsupported/contradicted/unable-to-compile/unable-to-verify across the live pipeline, using REAL evidence rather than a hypothetical benchmark, to prove the review-event architecture attaches at the right production boundaries.
methodologyNote: This phase does not run a new benchmark or select a new package (Section 23's own instruction). It reuses the deepest existing real evidence: (a) the already-computed evaluation-v2/atomic-contract cross-dataset regression across all 1,115 ground-truth units in FWRG/LSB/CONMED/DSGR (docs/evaluation-contract-v3/20-cross-dataset-regression.json, generated the same week from the identical frozen matcher), and (b) direct code inspection of each live pipeline stage's own already-computed failure/status taxonomy (SemanticCompilationStatus, SemanticVerificationStatus, SemanticCoverageState, DangerousUnaccountedReason, OperativeStateStatus). Both sources describe the SAME production pipeline this phase's safe-failure architecture attaches to.

livePipelineStages.canMaterialClaimBeLostHere: Yes - a candidate Phase 2B discovery never produces at all (NO_CANDIDATE_EVER_DISCOVERED in semantic-coverage's own DangerousUnaccountedReason vocabulary). This is the ONE failure class Section 31 places explicitly OUT OF SCOPE for the review-event architecture (an undiscovered claim), UNLESS semantic-coverage's own independent source-side inventory (Layer A/B/C) separately detects the same text as a MaterialSemanticUnit - in which case it is 'discovered' in the broader sense this architecture uses and is in scope.

livePipelineStages.ownFailureVocabulary: CTX-01/CTX-02 fixed in Phase 3F.1.4 (cross-referenced section's pending amendment now surfaced; wrong-context sibling contamination now requires subject-matter correspondence)
livePipelineStages.canMaterialClaimBeLostHere: Indirectly - insufficient/wrong context feeds into the compiler as MISSING_CONTEXT (a SemanticCompilerFailureReason) or SOURCE_CONTEXT_INCOMPLETE (a SemanticCoverageState), both already reviewable emission triggers downstream.

Yes - a claim whose operative text is ambiguous/conflicted downstream surfaces as OPERATIVE_STATE_UNRESOLVED (a SemanticCoverageState) or OPERATIVE_STATE_UNCERTAIN reasonCode. This phase's Workstream D additionally closes the gap where operative-state resolution did not compose structural health (see 14-operative-structural-health-audit.json).

Yes - this is the single richest existing failure taxonomy in the whole pipeline (11 distinct failure reasons), already never-silent by design (task §29's own 'explicit failure states, never a silent empty result'). Every one of these already maps cleanly onto semantic-coverage's downstream UNREPRESENTED/PARTIALLY_REPRESENTED/UNSUPPORTED coverage states once reconciliation runs.

Yes - a MATERIAL-severity, OPEN-resolutionStatus SemanticVerificationFinding is exactly a 'Headroom compiled something but the verifier contradicts it' event. Already structurally rich (findingId, sourceEvidence, sourceCitation, verifierReasoning - nearly a superset of what ClaimReviewItem needs); this phase's architecture reuses its role conceptually rather than duplicating its schema (see 03-safe-failure-architecture.json's own 'why not extend SemanticVerificationFinding directly' note).

This is the RECONCILIATION POINT where discovery+compiler+verifier evidence is already independently combined per material unit - the single existing computation that already answers 'was this specific claim safely represented' for every unit in its frozen source inventory. This phase's safe-failure architecture wires its ONE emission point here (see 05-emission-policy.json) precisely because it is the point where the other stages' evidence is ALREADY aggregated, avoiding duplicate/scattered emission logic across 5 separate call sites.

livePipelineStages.module: IR-level UNSUPPORTED_TYPE marker (lib/contract-model/ir/types.ts), surfaced as SemanticCoverageState.UNSUPPORTED
livePipelineStages.canMaterialClaimBeLostHere: Yes, but already never silent - an IR-inexpressible mechanic is a first-class marker value, not a dropped value; the coverage auditor already classifies it UNSUPPORTED. This phase's UNSUPPORTED_EXPRESSION reasonCode maps directly onto it.

realEvidenceFromCrossDatasetRegression.source: docs/evaluation-contract-v3/20-cross-dataset-regression.json (same frozen matcher, same week, real FWRG/LSB/CONMED/DSGR data)

aggregateFindings.note: 8 of 10 NO_CREDIT units in this small, well-covered document are dangerous silent omissions under the CURRENT (pre-this-phase) architecture - i.e. discovered/encountered but not specifically surfaced. These are exactly the population this phase's explicit review-event architecture targets.

CONMED is amendment-heavy and structurally the hardest package in the regression set (4-document package, one amendment target deliberately outside the package) - the highest absolute dangerous-silent-omission count of the four datasets.

The largest real dataset. 262 material claims currently have no explicit, claim-specific production record of Headroom's own uncertainty - this is the single largest concrete justification for this phase's mission.

realEvidenceFromCrossDatasetRegression.interpretation: Under the atomic-contract's own surfacingStatus dimension (Evaluation Contract V3), a 'dangerous silent omission' means NO_CREDIT + NOT_SPECIFICALLY_SURFACED - exactly the failure mode this phase's ClaimReviewItem architecture is built to eliminate by making the pipeline's own uncertainty an explicit, persisted, claim-specific record rather than something inferred indirectly. This 322-unit real population (not a synthetic estimate) is the concrete stakes of the NO_SILENT_MATERIAL_FAILURE invariant this phase introduces.

conclusionOnEmissionPointSelection: The coverage-auditor's own reconciliation output (SemanticUnitCoverageEntry + DangerousUnaccountedSemanticUnit) is the correct, minimal, single wiring point (Section 9's 'smallest set of production emission points necessary') because it is the ONE place in the live pipeline that already independently combines discovery+compiler+verifier+operative-state evidence per claim, before this phase ever writes a line of new emission logic. See 05-emission-policy.json for the exact derivation function and 03-safe-failure-architecture.json for why this generalizes rather than duplicates existing models.
